### Findings

**R2-F1 (S9; row).** `gov links` skips a relation whose changer is PROPOSED, REJECTED or WITHDRAWN (`NOT_A_CHANGER`). The removed loop reported those.
- Ordinary work: yes, because a PROPOSED entry carrying `**Supersedes:**` or `**Settles:**` is a normal draft.
- Consequence: other. An undecided or withdrawn entry changes nothing, so there is no unmarked change to lose. Once the entry is ACCEPTED, `gov links --all` reports it.

**R2-F2 (S9; Wave 3 row).** `unmarked()` treats the target as marked when its status line names the changer anywhere (`re.search` on `first`). The removed loop accepted only the status word or `**Changed by:**`. Planted F14 shows the gap: DEC-228's status line has `**Under:** DEC-229`, and DEC-229 settles DEC-228.
- Ordinary work: no, because an older entry's status line has to name its newer changer for some reason other than marking the change. The one real case (DEC-960) is in fact a mark.
- Consequence: fails open. Such an unmarked change would go unreported.
